9c63af3d34: Every block pays its reward to all miners together, split by the work each one does; here every computer is equally fast. One block a minute; the reward starts at 5 GNR and halves every 2,100,000 blocks (about every 4 years); at most 21,000,000 GNR will ever exist. Electricity and hardware are not counted.
594b8a0c22: Stock-to-flow: the GNR that exist divided by the new GNR mined in the next year, so how many years of mining are already stored. The higher it is, the rarer the coin. Gold is about {gold}. Every halving doubles it, and there will never be more than 21,000,000 GNR.
75c92504e4: As scarce as Bitcoin is today
387cbbacfb: Scarcity is a fact of the schedule; it does not set a price by itself. A coin is worth something only while people want it: scarcity decides how much of it each of them can have.

fc65e6fd6a: GNR only comes from mining. The more computers share the same reward, and the more halvings have passed, the more work one GNR takes. If a day of a computer's mining stays worth what it is worth today, one GNR is worth more in proportion.
